## ✅ What actually matters today

## 🌎 Major world changes
The global order is undergoing a structural realignment as private technology corporations increasingly underwrite geopolitical security and space infrastructure. The massive capital concentration in frontier AI firms—exemplified by Anthropic’s historic market debut and trillion-dollar valuations—has collided with sovereign monetary tightening, triggering severe equity corrections across New York, Tokyo, and Seoul. Concurrently, traditional multilateral frameworks are fracturing as bilateral defense and energy pacts bypass legacy institutions, highlighting a world where technological sovereignty dictates national power.

## 🎓 Today's lesson
**What is a Market Correction?**
A market correction is a downward movement of at least 10% in a stock index or asset price from its recent peak. Corrections are a normal part of economic cycles, acting like a pressure valve that releases speculative excess when asset prices rise faster than underlying company earnings. For example, if the S&P 500 index peaks at 7,000 and drops down to 6,300 due to rising interest rates or tech sell-offs, it has entered correction territory. While unnerving for everyday investors, historical data shows corrections happen frequently and are distinct from long-term bear markets (which involve drops of 20% or more).
